subsystems.name: Magnetic tap and guide array
subsystems.role: creates a controlled opening in the star's magnetic field and steers plasma toward the poles.
parts: superconducting coils sized in the thousands of kilometres

subsystems.name: Remote power supply
subsystems.role: provides the energy to start and sustain extraction, drawn from the star itself.

subsystems.name: Polar capture station
subsystems.role: sits at the magnetic pole to catch the outflowing plasma.

subsystems.name: Separation and storage plant
subsystems.role: sorts hydrogen, helium and trace metals and stores them.

subsystems.name: Control and monitoring network
subsystems.role: watches the star's activity and adjusts the extraction rate before the star destabilises.

buildSteps.title: Study the target star
buildSteps.detail: Decades of data on its magnetic cycle, rotation and convection are needed before any structure is placed, because the tap has to work with the star's own plasma flows rather than fight them.

buildSteps.title: Assemble the array off-world
buildSteps.detail: Coils and collectors are built in space from asteroid or lunar material, since launching them from Earth at this scale is impractical.

buildSteps.title: Position and hold the array
buildSteps.detail: The structure orbits close to the star or holds station above a pole, using light pressure and magnetic forces to stay in place despite the outward push of the star's wind.

buildSteps.title: Establish power
buildSteps.detail: Collector mirrors concentrate the star's own light to energise the magnets — the system must bootstrap itself, because nothing else can supply the required power.

buildSteps.title: Seed the magnetic tap
buildSteps.detail: A localised field is shaped in the photosphere, or a narrow beam ablates a small patch, raising a plume of plasma in the star's ~5,500 °C surface layers.

buildSteps.title: Channel and lift
buildSteps.detail: The magnetic nozzle guides the plume along field lines toward the pole, where the plasma is moving fast enough to be captured rather than falling back.

buildSteps.title: Capture and separate
buildSteps.detail: The polar station slows the plasma, extracts its heat, and separates hydrogen, helium and metals for storage or for use as reaction mass.

buildSteps.title: Sustain and regulate
buildSteps.detail: Extraction is held at a low fraction of the star's mass-loss and luminosity, with feedback that reduces the rate if the magnetic cycle or convection pattern shifts.

buildSteps.title: Exploit the result
buildSteps.detail: Lifted mass extends the star's main-sequence lifetime by removing the dense outer layers, supplies building material, and can be expelled as exhaust to move the entire system.

prerequisites.why: coils thousands of kilometres across must survive intense heat, radiation and mechanical force.
the hardware must be built and positioned without being launched from Earth.
predicting how a star reacts to having its outer layers drained is not yet reliable.
the whole operation must run without continuous human presence.
structures near a star need to shed enormous heat loads while staying intact.

pathway.milestone: helioseismology and solar physics missions mapping the Sun's interior and magnetic cycle
pathway.unlocks: the physics needed to predict how a star responds to any intervention.

pathway.milestone: robotic assembly of large structures in space from off-Earth materials
pathway.unlocks: the practical means to build anything on this scale.

pathway.milestone: a small-scale stellar tap that lifts a measurable but tiny flux from a star's polar region
pathway.unlocks: proof that magnetic extraction can be controlled rather than triggering instability.

pathway.milestone: sustained, regulated extraction on a star
pathway.unlocks: lifetime extension, bulk materials, and the ability to move a whole stellar system.
